title: Project Overview
description: Start with the README to understand the goal: predict the missing middle frame B from frames A and C using optical flow and occlusion-aware warping, then measure quality against ground truth.

title: Pipeline Entry Point
description: main.py orchestrates the whole Phase-1 run: extract -> triplets -> per-triplet baseline vs flow interpolation -> PSNR/SSIM report. Read it to see how the stages connect.

title: Preparing Data: Frames & Triplets
description: extract.py decodes the video into PNGs; triplets.py groups them into (A,B,C) sets where B is the ground-truth midpoint.

title: The Baseline to Beat
description: baseline.py just averages A and C. It has no motion awareness, so moving objects ghost — this is the reference the flow method must outperform.

title: Estimating Motion: Optical Flow
description: flow.py computes dense Farneback flow between frames and can visualize it as an HSV motion field.

title: Moving Pixels: Warping
description: warp.py remaps a frame along the flow to the midpoint. interpolate_with_flow warps A forward and C backward and averages them.

title: Handling Occlusions (The Core Idea)
description: interpolate.py adds the key trick: a forward-backward consistency mask down-weights pixels where the two flows disagree, then blends the two warps accordingly.

title: Measuring Quality
description: evaluate.py implements PSNR and SSIM from scratch to score predictions against ground truth.

title: Porting to a Native App
description: pipeline.cpp is the C++ video-to-video pipeline that interpolates every consecutive pair and writes a 2x-FPS output; main.cpp chooses between a headless CLI and the GUI.

title: The C++ Algorithm Ports
description: flow.cpp, warp.cpp, and blend.cpp mirror the Python stages using OpenCV in C++ — the CPU path of the native pipeline.

title: GPU Acceleration with CUDA
description: The CUDA kernels reimplement warp, blend, occlusion mask, and PSNR on the GPU. cuda_backend.cpp bridges OpenCV Mats to the extern-C host wrappers in app/cuda/.

title: The Desktop GUI
description: app.cpp runs the pipeline on a worker thread with thread-safe status; gui.cpp renders the Dear ImGui front-end with file pickers, controls, and a progress bar.

title: Building It All
description: CMakeLists.txt assembles the native app (fetching GLFW/ImGui, optional CUDA); the Makefile builds the standalone CUDA kernels into shared libraries.
